podcast.title: Adopting Hip Hop Profanity in Rock (1991)
podcast.body: On "Get In The Ring," Axl Rose "had picked up the unfiltered profanity of hip hop beef," directly challenging journalists who scrutinized his lyrics. However, he did so "without the syncopation or clever wordplay" typical of rap disses, illustrating a raw, confrontational rock approach to beef. "Axel Rose had picked up the unfiltered profanity of hip hop beef without the syncopation or clever wordplay."

podcast.title: Exceptional Vocal Range
podcast.body: Axl Rose possesses an exceptionally wide vocal range, which is noted to be greater than that of Freddie Mercury, Prince, and Mariah Carey. He is capable of hitting notes spanning over five and a half octaves. "Axel Rose has a wide vocal range, wider than Freddie Mercury prints and even Mariah Kerry. Axel Rose can hit notes over five and a half octaves."

xref.title: Four Lead Singers – Bon Scott Died 1980, Brian Johnson Made Back in Black, Axl Rose Subbed in 2016
xref.body: AC/DC has had four lead singers. Dave Evans was the original, present from the band's 1973 formation through their glam-rock phase. Bon Scott replaced him after being discovered working as the band's chauffeur; he recorded seven albums cementing AC/DC's reputation but died of acute alcohol poisoning on February 19, 1980. Brian Johnson replaced him in time for *Back in Black* (1980), which has sold at least 50 million copies. When Johnson developed serious ear problems in 2016, Axl Rose of Guns N' Roses sang for approximately two dozen shows; Johnson subsequently received treatment and rejoined. "The swap worked way better than anyone could have dreamed."

xref.title: 1992 MTV Music Video Awards Altercation
xref.body: The animosity between Nirvana and Guns N' Roses culminated in a backstage altercation at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards. Axl Rose confronted Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love, reportedly telling Kurt to "keep his woman in line." Simultaneously, Nirvana bassist Chris Novoselic and Guns N' Roses bassist Duff McKagan were also arguing. "This boiled over to an altercation backstage at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards between Axel, Kurt and Courtney Love."

xref.title: Axl Rose Using Dave Grohl's Throne
xref.body: In 2016, Axl Rose borrowed Dave Grohl's custom-built throne (which Grohl had used while touring with a broken leg) after Axl himself broke a bone in his foot, indicating a thawing of past hostilities between members of the two bands. "In fact, back in 2016, when Axel had a broken bone in his foot, he borrowed Dave Grohl's throne, the one he used to tour when Dave broke his leg."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Connection to Axl Rose
xref.body: Shannon Hoon's sister knew Axl Rose from Indiana, which led to Hoon securing a gig singing backup vocals for Guns N' Roses. He contributed to several songs on their "Use Your Illusion" CDs and can be seen in the music video for "Don't Cry." "For example, singer Shannon Hoon's sister knew this guy from Indiana named Axel Rose, and one thing led to another, and Shannon got a gig singing backup vocals for Guns and Roses."

xref.title: Connection to Guns n' Roses
xref.body: Shannon Hoon's sister was friends with Axl Rose during high school in Indiana, which led to Shannon singing backup vocals on a couple of Guns n' Roses songs and appearing in the "Don't Cry" video. "Shannon ended up in the Guns and Roses orbit because his sister had been friends with Axel Rose back in high school in Indiana."

xref.title: Dave Grohl's On-Stage Taunt
xref.body: Following the backstage confrontation at the 1992 MTV Music Video Awards, Nirvana performed. Towards the end of their performance, Dave Grohl reportedly taunted Axl Rose from the stage on live television. "Now, hold on to the very end when Dave Grohl comes to the mic and taunts Axel from the stage on live TV."

xref.title: Feud with Guns N' Roses
xref.body: The bad blood between Nirvana and Guns N' Roses, particularly with Axl Rose, started when Kurt Cobain refused an offer for Nirvana to open for Guns N' Roses on a major world tour. Kurt viewed Guns N' Roses as "too big" and was concerned that aligning with them would be perceived as selling out, stating Nirvana was not a "typical Guns n' Roses type of band that has absolutely nothing to say." Axl Rose, who was a fan of Nirvana (even wearing a Nirvana hat in the "Don't Cry" video), felt snubbed and began publicly insulting Kurt and Courtney Love as "junkies," claiming their daughter had birth defects due to their drug use. "It began when Kurt refused an offer by the Gunners to have Nirvana open for them on one of their massive world tours."

xref.title: Feud with Nirvana
xref.body: The animosity began when Nirvana refused an offer to open for Guns N' Roses on a major world tour, a decision Kurt Cobain made due to concerns about being perceived as "sellouts" and his disdain for what he called the "typical Guns n' Roses type of band that has absolutely nothing to say." Axl Rose, a fan of Nirvana who even wore a Nirvana hat in the "Don't Cry" video, felt insulted and began publicly calling Kurt and Courtney Love "junkies," claiming their daughter had birth defects due to their drug use. "It began when Kurt refused an offer by the Gunners to have Nirvana open for them on one of their massive world tours."

xref.title: Public Insults Against Axl Rose
xref.body: In late 1992, Kurt Cobain gave an interview where he publicly denounced Axl Rose, calling him "a sexist and a racist and a homophobic" and stating that one could not be on Guns N' Roses' side and Nirvana's side simultaneously, further adding that Guns N' Roses "can't write good music." "Axel is a sexist and a racist and a homophobic. And you can't be on his side and be on our side."
